title: Assign Jira issues with AI by a teammate’s name
h1: give a jira issue to the teammate you name
description: Ask an AI bot to assign a Jira issue by name or email, use the project default or clear an owner. Handle ambiguous matches before any assignment changes.
answer: tell a bot which jira issue needs an owner and who should take it. it can find the issue, look up the teammate by name or email and change the assignment. it can also use the project's default assignee or leave an issue unassigned. this is a write action, so sending approval does not cover it; put an ask-first instruction in any assignment routine.
og_line: an owner chosen by your routing rule.
what:
assignment changes who owns an existing issue. the bot can search jira for the issue you describe and use the action's name or email lookup for the person you mean. when a name is unclear, find users 2 can help it show you candidate accounts.

the project default and no assignee are different choices. leaving the assignee out can clear the assignment, so a failed person lookup should stop the job. it should never quietly become a request to unassign the issue.
uses: route a newly reported billing bug to the person covering that queue
transfer a specific ticket after both teammates agree on the handoff
return a misrouted issue to the project's default owner
clear an assignment when the team explicitly wants the work back in its unassigned queue

routine.message: at 10 each weekday, find unassigned issues in the invoicing project whose title or description mentions 'tax receipt'. propose assigning them to devin rowe, using the workspace user match rather than guessing from a first name. bring the issue titles and proposed owner here and ask before changing any assignment. after i confirm, assign only those issues and report them here; never clear an owner or substitute a different teammate if the lookup fails.
routine.needs: jira connected, with read and write access for this bot
routine.output:
routing approved and applied

inv-51: tax receipt missing for larkspire co.
new owner: devin rowe.

inv-58 kept unassigned because its routing decision was not approved.

steps: open jira in **Connected apps** and give this routing bot **read and write** permission.
describe the project, selection rule and intended teammate; ask for the matched account before the first assignment.
limit allowed actions to issue searching, user lookup and assignment, and include 'ask before changing any assignment' in the scheduled request.
inspect the first routing result in jira; choose **Pause** on the routine card when cover changes or the rule expires.
watch: jira cloud privacy settings can prevent a name or email lookup. the bot should report the failed match instead of choosing someone else.
omitting the intended assignee can remove the current owner. a missing match is a reason to stop, not a fallback assignment.
read only cannot assign issues. with write access, **Ask every time** for sending does not itself hold assignments for review.
multiple people can share a display name; compare the candidate accounts before applying the routing rule.

faq.q: can i assign a jira ticket using just an email address?
faq.a: the action supports email or display-name lookup. if jira's privacy settings block the search, the bot can try finding the user account and ask you to confirm the match.

faq.q: is the default assignee the same as unassigned?
faq.a: no. one choice routes the issue to the project's default owner; the other removes the current owner. say which outcome you want in plain words.

faq.q: will it ask me before reassigning tickets?
faq.a: only when you instruct it to do so. assignments are changes inside jira, and the separate sending approval does not make them wait.
